correctness.rationale: Explicit uniform-source conditional enumeration gives exact leaf and hub expectations and two pair joint moments. Covariance subtraction factors into claimed polynomials. Hub–leaf quadratic is strictly increasing on nonnegative transmission; leaf–leaf cubic is strictly convex and changes sign at most once after its initial decline. Difference polynomials have positive concave bracket on [0,1], proving strict order and threshold ordering. Rescaling each polynomial gives the two asserted limits. Every finite checker result follows from independent full source/edge-state enumeration and does not stand in for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The verified claim is the full two-pair covariance classification for independently retained star edges and exactly one uniformly random source, with strict pair ordering and distinct large-star scaling exponents. Primary epidemic percolation and detection papers address forward spread/detection or optimization rather than these second-moment phases; the relevant instantaneous-SIR correlation counterexample uses a different observable. Potential earlier positive-association results with fixed/product initial laws do not automatically imply an exactly-one-source mixture. Full-text access to one plausible older correlation source was unavailable; this is a documented residual risk rather than proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: Pairwise outbreak-alarm agreement is a natural surveillance reliability and corroboration quantity distinct from expected alarm count and probability that at least one monitor activates. A full classification of the two geometrically distinct pair types gives an exact opposite-sign range, sharp unique transition points for all star degrees, and nontrivially different scaling orders as hub degree grows. This identifies how uniform source selection and transmission interact at different graph distances and is a motivated structural theorem rather than a numerical artifact.
